clue.text: Keep rapping: that may lead to a scrum

definitions.text: that may lead to a scrum

blocks.note: first meaning: a phrasal verb, to go on hammering at a door

blocks.clueFragment: that may lead to a scrum
blocks.note: second meaning: in rugby, dropping the ball forward is an offence restarted with a scrum

explanation.surface: Someone told to go on rapping at a door, as though the noise might start a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a knock-on is fumbling the ball forwards, and the usual penalty is a scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means continue hitting, and the hyphenated noun is the rugby handling error punished by a scrum.

clue.text: Less comfortable indoors, young relative takes in US state one part at a time

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside yourself, so the relative surrounds the state
the state's abbreviation goes in piecemeal, each letter slotted into a different gap

blocks.note: a daughter is a young relative
postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A girl absorbing the facts about an American state bit by bit, while feeling chilly at home.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes in after the D and I after the T, so DAUGHTER becomes DRAUGHTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughty room lets in cold currents of air, making an interior less cosy; this is the comparative form.

clue.text: Agree not to vote, even in France

blocks.note: first meaning: MPs on opposing sides arrange to abstain together so their absences cancel out
second meaning: the French word for an even number

explanation.surface: An abstention pact that is apparently made even across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pairing is a Westminster custom: two MPs from opposing parties both stay away from a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary pairing is a mutual abstention arrangement, and the French adjective pair describes numbers divisible by two.

clue.text: Overgrown with prickles, front of house is with predictable exceptions totally covered

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
the exceptions fall at a regular, predictable spacing, so every other letter is dropped
something covered has a layer wrapped round it, so letters go inside

blocks.note: opening letter of house
taken as written
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of totally

explanation.surface: A neglected garden in front of the house, almost entirely smothered in weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: HIS sits between the first T and the TLY of the alternate letters, giving T-HIS-TLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thistles are prickly weeds, so ground thick with them is covered in spiky growth; the adjective is rare but regular.

clue.text: Madman in church starts to rebuke several people unable to keep quiet

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it
the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: as mad as a hatter, after Carroll's Mad Hatter
Church of England
first letters of rebuke and several

explanation.surface: A lunatic in church, and the congregation must tell off the people who will not shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatterers are folk who talk incessantly, so a group of them cannot stay silent; the plural matches.

clue.text: One bird following another

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
another bird, an example

explanation.surface: Birdwatching: one bird trailing behind a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' borrows bird from the definition: it means another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl is a general word for a bird, especially poultry or game, so it names a single feathered creature.

clue.text: Repairman captures a snake

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it within your grasp

blocks.note: someone who mends things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handyman catching a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' is a verb here, not the reptile the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or river that snakes winds in loops, and to meander is to follow such a twisting course.

clue.text: After short dash caught fish that’s come too close

indicators.note: after says which pieces come later, so the short dash goes first

blocks.note: an en dash is the shorter typographic dash
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler who, after a quick sprint, lands a fish that strayed too near.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude gradually onto another's ground, moving nearer than is welcome; infinitive matches.

clue.text: Does some housework, run off feet

indicators.note: something taken off is removed and no longer there

blocks.note: hoovering is vacuum cleaning, from the Hoover brand
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone vacuuming, then running off their feet with chores.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is the British everyday verb for vacuuming. Removing R from HOOVERS leaves HOOVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooves are the horny feet of horses, cattle and similar animals, so the plural noun fits feet.

clue.text: Comes into lots of land: who from abroad is squatting?

indicators.note: a squatter occupies a building, living inside it

blocks.note: acres are units of land area
the French word for who

explanation.surface: Someone inheriting estates, and asking which foreigner is occupying them illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into something is to obtain it, typically through inheritance, and acquires means gains possession of.

clue.text: Gift of story book

blocks.note: a tale is a story
New Testament, the usual crossword book

explanation.surface: Receiving a storybook as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift can mean a natural aptitude, and talent is an innate ability or flair.

clue.text: Spread animosity at uni, filthy swine? I already knew about that

indicators.note: filthy suggests things messed up and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to sow seed is to spread it
hate is strong animosity
the London School of Economics, a university
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgusting pig at university stirring up ill will, and the reply that this is old news.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread is a verb (sow seed), not a feast; the LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sarcastic retort meaning this is nothing surprising, exactly what someone says when they knew already.

clue.text: Interpreter cis for now, might we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we might hear says the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: someone currently cisgender might be trans at a later time

explanation.surface: A question about gender identity changing over time, wrapped in a nod to interpreting.
explanation.walkthrough: Cis and trans are opposites; being cis for now implies trans later.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpreter renders speech or writing from one language into another, which is what a translator does.

clue.text: Pouch closed, filled with noodle soup: capital!

indicators.note: something filled with an item has that item inside it

blocks.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in a body
a door pushed to is shut
ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

explanation.surface: A sealed bag of instant noodle soup, greeted with a cheer of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' sounds like an old-fashioned exclamation of delight, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, a city that is the seat of state government.

clue.text: Competitor, one who has turned up without filling in card

indicators.note: the filling of a word is the part inside its outer letters
without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: an arrival is a person who has come
the two inner letters of card

explanation.surface: A rival who appeared without completing the entry card.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping AR from the start of ARRIVAL leaves RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival is someone contending against another for the same prize or goal, so a fellow competitor.

clue.text: Check on a rod for fish

blocks.note: per means a, as in a pound a head
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An angler checking the rod while waiting for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means comes after. A perch is an old unit of length, also called a rod or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is both a measure of length identical to a rod and a common spiny-finned freshwater fish.

clue.text: Change a nasty sweet filling

indicators.note: a nasty turn of events leaves things in a mess, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Swapping out a horrible confectionery centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'nasty' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganache is a mixture of chocolate and cream used to fill cakes and truffles, a sweet filling.

clue.text: In part of joint, a thousand erotic moves

indicators.note: moves suggests shifting position, so the letters change places

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestive picture of a thousand saucy moves in a smoky joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is carpentry here, not a club or a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortice is the hole cut in timber to receive a tenon, one half of the mortice-and-tenon woodwork join.

clue.text: Two infusions to finish off menu in country house

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: cha (slang for tea) plus tea
last letter of menu

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea at a stately home, with two cups to round off the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (or char) is an old British slang word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large manor in the countryside, a grand rural residence.

clue.text: Tusker has to be in pain, carrying round this on the face?

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

blocks.note: a walrus has prominent tusks
must means has to
O is round in shape
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: An elephant in agony, and a question about what this face is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tusker' suggests an elephant but leads to the walrus, whose whiskers name the face furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick, drooping growth over the upper lip, resembling the animal's whiskers.

clue.text: Gap that all can see in ruined canal

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape
one thing being in another means it sits inside

blocks.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A breach in a derelict canal, visible to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: U-rated films in Britain are suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacuna is a missing section or blank space, especially in a manuscript or argument, so a gap.

clue.text: Some beautiful Namibians, one on each arm

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words that follow is used

blocks.note: the end of beautiful and start of Namibians

explanation.surface: Beautiful Namibian people, each with a companion on their arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones, so every arm has exactly one.

clue.text: Abjuring alcohol, holding parties sadly’s ending in farce

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within your grip
the ending of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: teetotal
raves are dance parties
last letter of sadly

explanation.surface: A teetotaller throwing parties, which sadly ends in a fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, describes someone who does not drink alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque misrepresentation, and a farce is a mockery of something serious.

clue.text: A wife always on holiday?

blocks.note: taken as written
w is the abbreviation for wife
ay, or aye, is an archaic word for always

explanation.surface: A spouse who seems to be permanently on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off on vacation is not at home or work but elsewhere, which is what being away means.

clue.text: Hours on knees ultimately enthusiastic about ancestor worship

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the very end, the final letter

blocks.note: last letter of knees
h is the abbreviation for hours
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Spending hours kneeling, finally keen on venerating forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts hours after the end of knees.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the native Japanese religion, centred on veneration of kami, including the spirits of ancestors.

clue.text: Put hands together on mouth creating gibberish

blocks.note: applauding by striking palms
slang for mouth, as in shut your trap

explanation.surface: Someone clapping a hand over a mouth that is spouting nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious or empty talk, nonsense speech aimed at winning applause, so meaningless chatter.
